title: .happy-env.json
description: Local development environment for a WordPress project. The repo is a wp-content directory; this file says how to run it.

php.description: PHP version. Must exist as a wordpress:<wordpress>-php<php>-apache image tag.

wordpress.description: WordPress version. A minor like '6.9' resolves to its latest patch when a site is first created; a full version like '6.9.4' pins exactly. An existing site keeps the core it was created with until it is destroyed.

core.description: A full WordPress checkout to run instead of the image's core, relative to the repo (absolute paths work). It is bind-mounted whole as the docroot and supplies wp-content, so themes, plugins, muPlugins and root cannot be set with it; `mounts` may only replace files that already exist in the checkout. The `wordpress` key then only picks the image's PHP and Apache.

host.description: Hostname for a single-site repo, e.g. 'mysite.example.dev'. Must resolve to the proxy; see the README on DNS. Shorthand for a one-entry `sites`. Mutually exclusive with `sites`.

aliases.description: Additional hostnames routed to this site, for a repo whose WordPress network serves more than one domain. `host` stays the canonical URL; these only have to route.

themes.description: Theme directories to mount, relative to the site root. Defaults to every directory in ./themes.

plugins.description: Plugins to install. A wordpress.org slug ('woocommerce'), an optionally versioned slug ('woocommerce@10.7.0'), a zip URL, or a local path ('./plugins/my-plugin').

muPlugins.description: Directory whose entries are each mounted into wp-content/mu-plugins, relative to the site root. Defaults to ./mu-plugins when present.

mounts.description: Extra paths to mount into wp-content, as { source: target }. Sources are relative to the site root, targets to wp-content — e.g. { "./vendor": "vendor" } for a composer directory that plugins in the repo autoload from. An absolute target is a path anywhere in the container, e.g. "/etc/apache2/conf-enabled/site.conf".

fallback.description: Production origin, e.g. 'https://mysite.com'. Any uploads file missing from the local bind mount is reverse-proxied from '<fallback>/wp-content/uploads/…', so a dev site runs against real media without syncing it.

sites.description: Sites in this repo, keyed by slug. The slug names the database and container. Use this instead of `host` when one repo serves several sites.

aliases.description: Additional hostnames routed to this site, for a network serving more than one domain.

root.description: Site root relative to the repo, when a site's wp-content is not the repo root.

core.description: A full WordPress checkout to run instead of the image's core, relative to the repo. See the top-level `core`.
